flashcard_questions.q: What is the purpose of a script?
flashcard_questions.a: To give the cast and crew everything they need to perform and film each scene.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the purpose of a storyboard?
flashcard_questions.a: To plan the sequence of shots in a moving-image product visually.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a slug line in a script?
flashcard_questions.a: The scene heading, written in capitals.

flashcard_questions.q: What do the abbreviations INT. and EXT. show in a scene heading?
flashcard_questions.a: Whether the scene is interior or exterior.

flashcard_questions.q: In what tense is the action description of a script written?
What is a parenthetical direction in a script?
flashcard_questions.a: A bracketed note showing how a line should be delivered.

flashcard_questions.q: Where is a character's name placed in a script?
flashcard_questions.a: Centred and in capitals above their dialogue.

flashcard_questions.q: Which script transition instructs an instant change to the next scene?

flashcard_questions.a: A breakdown of each scene listing all the props and equipment needed.

flashcard_questions.q: Which storyboard component records how long a shot lasts?
What do the panels of a storyboard look like?
flashcard_questions.a: A comic strip of drawn images.

flashcard_questions.q: Which media product would not need a storyboard?
Why do actors and camera operators read different parts of a script?
flashcard_questions.a: Each person focuses on the information relevant to their own role.

notes: 13 cards: 2 document-to-purpose, 6 script convention cards, 3 storyboard cards, 1 application, 1 causal. Script component lists were split into single-convention cards rather than one stuffed answer.
